title: Against Celsus, Book II
blurb: Origen answers the Jew whom Celsus brings on stage to speak against the Jews who believe in Jesus, and shows that they have not left the law of their fathers. He goes on to defend Jesus’ foreknowledge of his betrayal, the reality of his suffering and death, and his resurrection, and argues that no mere man could have won so much of the world.
first_english_note: Earlier English: Frederick Crombie (Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1872) and Henry Chadwick (1953). This is a fresh English translation from Koetschau’s Greek; neither was used as wording.

text_history.method: Copy-text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI. The English is a fresh translation from that Greek, chapter by chapter (2.1–79), with an independent clause-by-clause review against the Greek. Crombie and Chadwick were not used.
